selection.policy: Screen relative visual orbits, then require reviewed component identities, a credible barycentre and an adopted mass ratio. Infrared-only magnitudes and unknown component magnitudes do not pass automatically. Hierarchical pairs require explicit scope. Existing 14 examples remain labelled exceptions where appropriate.

systems.name: Castor
systems.note: Outer A–B orbit only; the inner spectroscopic pairs and Castor C are not modelled. Absolute astrometry is anchored to Hipparcos component A.
systems.review: USNO grade 3 CIA2022d outer orbit. Adopted subsystem masses, distance and systemic velocity/proper motion come from Stellarium 26.3. Hipparcos I/239 HIP 36850 has AstroRef=A, so the component-A orbital displacement is removed from its J1991.25 position to obtain the barycentre anchor. Gaia DR3 G=2.925 identifies B; its shared AT-HYG Gaia alias is assigned only to B. Catalogue and adopted systemic-motion uncertainties limit absolute positions.

systems.name: Procyon
systems.note: The Hipparcos 1997 '+' astrometric reference is the centre of mass at J1991.25. Component positions are derived from that barycentre; no primary orbital motion is added to catalogue proper motion.
systems.review: USNO grade 3 BdH2015. Masses, adopted 285.0 mas parallax and -4.115 km/s systemic velocity follow Bond et al. (2015). Barycentric position and proper motion come from Hipparcos I/239 HIP 37279, AstroRef='+', MultFlag='O'. The astrometric anchor retains catalogue uncertainty; the relative orbit is independently checked against USNO ephemerides.

systems.name: 70 Ophiuchi
systems.review: USNO grade 1 Izm2019 orbit and adopted masses 0.9/0.7 from Stellarium 26.3. Absolute astrometry is the mass-weighted Gaia DR3 component solution at J2016.0. Stellarium uses a J2000 label for essentially J2016 component data; the original reference epoch is preserved here. Median component radial velocities are adopted, with catalogue limitations.
systems.note: Barycentre derived from the two resolved Gaia DR3 sources at their actual J2016.0 reference epoch, with adopted component masses 0.9/0.7.

systems.name: μ Cassiopeiae
systems.massRatioNote: Bond et al. 2020 dynamical masses, adopted parallax and systemic radial velocity; visual pair Aa–Ab (also called A–B), with no additional inner orbit modelled.
systems.review: USNO grade 2 BdH2020 relative orbit. Hipparcos I/239 AstroRef=+, MultFlag=O supplies the barycentric position and proper motion at J1991.25. Bond et al. 2020 dynamical masses, adopted parallax and systemic radial velocity; visual pair Aa–Ab (also called A–B), with no additional inner orbit modelled. Absolute astrometry retains the uncertainty of the original Hipparcos orbital solution.
systems.note: Bond et al. 2020 dynamical masses, adopted parallax and systemic radial velocity; visual pair Aa–Ab (also called A–B), with no additional inner orbit modelled.

systems.name: β Coronae Borealis
systems.massRatioNote: Muterspaugh et al. 2010 Table 5 and section IV.2.3 dynamical masses and S99 parallax. Systemic RV is left unknown: the paper fits separate instrumental velocity offsets; the existing catalogue RV is a component measurement.
systems.review: USNO grade 1 Mut2010b relative orbit. Hipparcos I/239 AstroRef=+, MultFlag=O supplies the barycentric position and proper motion at J1991.25. Muterspaugh et al. 2010 Table 5 and section IV.2.3 dynamical masses and S99 parallax. Systemic RV is left unknown: the paper fits separate instrumental velocity offsets; the existing catalogue RV is a component measurement. Absolute astrometry retains the uncertainty of the original Hipparcos orbital solution.
systems.note: Muterspaugh et al. 2010 Table 5 and section IV.2.3 dynamical masses and S99 parallax. Systemic RV is left unknown: the paper fits separate instrumental velocity offsets; the existing catalogue RV is a component measurement.

systems.name: 80 Tauri
systems.massRatioNote: Torres 2019 dynamical component masses (posterior modes 1.63/1.11 solar masses); adopted parallax and fitted barycentric proper motion from Table 3.
systems.review: USNO grade 3 Trr2019 relative orbit. Component identities are the resolved Gaia DR3 and Tycho-2 pair. Barycentre position is mass-weighted from Gaia DR3 at its actual J2016.0 epoch; distance and systemic proper motion follow Torres (2019) Table 3, rather than reusing component proper motion. Adopted masses are rounded posterior modes, not an independent high-precision absolute calibration. Systemic radial velocity remains unknown. The orbit predicts the independent Gaia separation vector within 0.015 arcsec.
systems.note: Two-component 80 Tau model. Published component masses have appreciable uncertainty; grade 3 orbit and fixed absolute motion remain approximate. No systemic RV is adopted, so perspective acceleration is omitted.
